hook: Telangana, AP fight over Krishna water with *no* full meter
hook_b: Telangana, AP fight over Krishna water with *no* full meter
tldr: The Krishna River Management Board has no complete real-time system to show how much water Telangana and Andhra Pradesh each draw.

beats.what: Phase I installed 18 telemetry stations, including at Jurala, Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam; phases II (9) and III (11) never started.
beats.why: Phase II stalled because AP did not release its share of the ₹9 crore, per Telangana officials.
beats.care: The contractor's five-year maintenance deal for the 18 stations ends on Dec 26; neither state has replied to KRMB's letters.

causes.label: AP didn't release its share of funds

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: In 2024-25, AP used 718 tmc and Telangana 288 tmc of the 1,006 tmc drawn from the Krishna, per the KRMB annual report.

cards.q: Who should pay to finish Krishna water metering?

qs: Without shared real-time data, how can either state's claims about overdrawal be checked?

facts.t: Phase II needed *₹9 crore*; Telangana released ₹4.5 crore, AP's matching share never came, officials said.

viz.verdict: AP drew about 71% of the total, per the KRMB annual report.

learn.t: KRMB = Krishna River Management Board, which manages Krishna water sharing between Telangana and AP

watch: KRMB's next meetings on the stalled network and who maintains stations after Dec 26.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: No accurate measure of Krishna water use as Telangana, AP spar

fact: KRMB still can't measure Krishna water use; only *18* telemetry stations exist
twist: Telangana's ₹4.5 crore for new stations was spent by KRMB on office upkeep and salaries, a Telangana official said.
